To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

retrieval practice is more effective than restudy and the benefits of retrieval practice are greater with longer study-test lages and with feedback, particularly for students with lower ability (lower working memory capacity).

(1) the benefits from retrieval for lower ability students is greater when feedback is given and the study-test lag is greater; and (2) for lower ability students, the benefits from retrieval with feedback are greater than those from retrieval without feedback.

(i) retrieval practice is an effective learning method for both high and low working memory capacity students, and (ii) for lower working memory capacity students the benefits of retrieval practice are greater when feedback is given after the initial test.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: How does retrieval practice affect the learning of lower ability students, and how does it compare with other learning strategies?
the effects of retrieval on memory, and in particular, the effects of testing on subsequent memory.
understanding how the effects of retrieval-based learning are influenced by the spacing between study and test trials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the benefits of retrieval practice were more evident in lower WM capacity students, particularly with longer study-test lages and with the inclusion of feedback.
retrieval practice is a very effective strategy for learning for both high and low working memory capacity students, but that the effects are greater for low working memory capacity individuals.

(1) retrieval practice is more effective than restudy, particularly when there is a delay between study and retrieval; (2) the benefits from retrieval are greater for students who have lower working memory capacity; (3) the benefits from feedback are greater when retrieval is spaced in time, particularly for students with lower ability; (4) the benefits from spaced retrieval with feedback are greater for students of lower working memory capacity, but only when the delay between study and the final test is relatively long;
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the benefits of retrieval practice are greater when retrieval is delayed and when feedback is given.
retrieval practice is a good strategy for learning, and it is particularly effective for low working memory capacity students.
retrieval practice with feedback, particularly after longer lags, benefits students who are less able to benefit from restudying.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of retrieval-based learning are not always straightforward.
retrieval practice is a useful tool for students who are struggling with learning and remembering material.
the effects of retrieval-based learning are more complex and nuanced than has been previously thought.
